neighbours.label: In cell / developmental biology prose, the naming or copula word (is called a, known as, becomes, appear as) just before a technical term or description; the same construction outside biology is quiet
fire: Once the sperm enters, the fertilized egg is called a zygote and begins to divide.
By the third week the embryo folds into three layers, which are known as the germ layers.
As the oocyte matures, the nucleus becomes larger and the surrounding cells multiply.
The outer layer of the early embryo is called the trophoblast and later forms the placenta.
During mitosis the chromatin condenses and each chromosome becomes visible as a pair of chromatids.
The solid ball of sixteen cells produced by cleavage is known as a morula.
In the testis, the immature germ cells are called spermatogonia and lie along the tubule wall.
After gastrulation the innermost cell layer is termed the endoderm and gives rise to the gut.
quiet: Once the bill passes, the amended text is called a statute and begins to apply.
By the third week the recruits split into three squads, which are known as the watch teams.
As the evening wears on, the crowd becomes larger and the nearby streets fill up.
The outer wall of the old castle is called the curtain and later formed the town boundary.
During the thaw the snow softens and each footpath becomes visible as a dark line on the hill.
The heavy loaf of rye bread baked by the monks is known as a miche.
Sperm swim through the cervix and uterus, and one of them finally fuses with the egg.
The embryo implants in the wall of the uterus about a week after fertilization.
